correctness.rationale: For an omitted vertex in part \(V_i\), the selected-neighbor count is exactly \(s-s_i\) and the unselected-neighbor count is \(N-n_i-(s-s_i)\). Thus the defining inequality is equivalent to \(s-s_i\ge\lceil(N-n_i+k)/2\rceil\); for positive \(k\) it also forces domination. The coefficient-extraction formula then counts allowed part profiles with their binomial multiplicities. A fresh independent literal-neighborhood replay on all complete-multipartite profiles through order six and all admissible positive \(k\) matched the criterion. The infinite theorem is the exact neighbor-count identity.
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to the standard positive range \(1\le k\le\Delta\); negative \(k\) is not covered.
